questions.q: Which slice supplies scores for the next continuation token from logits shaped batch by time by vocabulary?
questions.why: The last input position predicts the token after the complete current context.

questions.q: What does lowering a positive temperature do for a fixed row of unequal finite logits?
choices: Amplifies relative probability differences without changing the logit ranking
questions.why: The odds ratio is exp((z_i-z_j)/T). Positive scaling preserves score order and does not train parameters.

questions.q: What does top-k equal to 1 do under this lab's tie policy?
choices: Keeps one maximum-score candidate, matching greedy decoding
questions.why: Only the maximum remains; stable lower-ID tie breaking agrees with the greedy branch.

questions.q: At top-p 0.7, which candidates survive probabilities [0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.125]?
questions.why: A alone has mass 0.5. Including B reaches 0.75, so the crossing token B must remain before renormalizing.

questions.q: For logits log([4, 2, 1, 1]), predict the probabilities at temperature 0.5.
questions.why: Dividing the log weights by one half doubles them, so exponentiation squares the original weights.

questions.q: The block size is 128, the prompt has 130 tokens, and generation requests two new tokens with no EOS. Predict the context_lengths and returned length.
questions.why: The loop crops only the view passed to the model. It preserves the full prompt and appends both generated IDs.

questions.q: Explain why the tree with first probabilities A=0.6, B=0.4 and best continuations 0.51 after A and 0.99 after B defeats greedy sequence maximization.
rubric: Greedy path has probability 0.306 but the B path has probability 0.396
A locally highest-probability choice need not give the globally highest-probability sequence
Sequence likelihood is still not a guarantee of human usefulness or truth

questions.q: Design a fair comparison of decoding policies and explain why one attractive output does not prove that a policy is better.
rubric: Hold checkpoint, tokenizer and prompt set fixed; do not update weights
Vary one policy control at a time when attributing a causal effect
Record environment, seed, policy order and token/stopping budgets
Use multiple prompts and samples and judge task-relevant correctness rather than only style
Explain that sampled tokens change context, not trained parameters
Separate repeatability from correctness and avoid claiming cross-platform exact replay

questions.q: Why does the helper require model.eval() as well as inference mode?
choices: Inference mode does not disable dropout by switching model mode
questions.why: Evaluation mode controls training-dependent modules. Inference mode controls autograd bookkeeping; PyTorch documents these as separate.

questions.q: For probabilities [0.6, 0.25, 0.15], predict the survivors under top-p=0.7 alone versus top-k=2 followed by top-p=0.7.
questions.answer: Top-p alone keeps the first two. Top-k then top-p keeps only the first.
questions.why: After top-k renormalization the first probability is 0.705882, already above the nucleus threshold.

recall.q: What is the autoregressive generation loop?
recall.a: Compute logits for the current context, select the last position, apply a decoding policy, choose one token, append it, and repeat until a stop condition.

recall.q: Does lower temperature make an answer true?
recall.a: No. It sharpens relative sampling probabilities for fixed logits; it neither updates weights nor checks facts.

recall.q: What is the crossing-token rule in nucleus sampling?
recall.a: Keep the smallest highest-probability prefix that reaches or exceeds the threshold, including the token that crosses it, then renormalize.

recall.q: What does a seed guarantee here?
recall.a: Replay in the tested fixed environment with the same checkpoint, prompt and policy, not universal equality across devices or software releases.

recall.q: Why is a maximum-new-token limit still needed with EOS?
recall.a: The model may never produce EOS; the token budget provides a bounded stopping condition.
